families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

meaning: Each tie is a pointer that landed. Whether the paper and the Lean say the same thing is a reading.

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem gives both whole-space and torus breakdown under the complete cell condition. This is the conditional implication stated in the opening sentence.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.spaceAndTorusBreakdown_of_cell_system_condition

rows.fidelity_note: The condition is the fifteen-clause premise of that implication. A numerical witness satisfying it is a separate obligation.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The condition has fifteen direct clauses over the seven shared choices of cell data, field instances, local calculations, tree, assembly, constants and reduction data. The sentence counts these choices correctly.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: Only used row coordinates are constrained by the common real row variables and complex gauge and pressure-head terms. All unused and port coordinates are free complex numbers, and both actuator blocks are required to be real.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange

rows.fidelity_note: The retained potential inequality is quantified over every vector satisfying the supplied admissibility condition. In the final cell condition that is the complete compatible-row space described immediately before this sentence.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The retained pairing inequality is quantified over every admissible vector. Substituting the final compatible-row condition gives the full domain stated in the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The residual elimination comparison is quantified over every admissible vector. It therefore includes the free and gauge directions of the full compatible-row condition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The missing-breakpoint default R makes each affected support guard true because R ≤ |R|. A node coefficient needs one guard and a bubble coefficient needs both endpoint guards; when both endpoints are absent, the bubble coefficient is therefore forced to zero.
rows.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.VanishesBeyond

rows.fidelity_note: The actuator-model measurability and weighted-square-integrability condition quantifies over every natural index. It is broader than a check restricted to the finitely many physical actuators.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowFunctionalConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The node conversion uses the inverse scale with missing scales replaced by 1. Its formula remains defined at scale zero, as the passage says.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetAxis.convert

rows.fidelity_note: The scale condition requires equality of list lengths and invariance under reversal. It does not require any scale to be nonzero.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasSymmetricScale

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels
ties.plain: Model harmonics active in a cell

rows.fidelity_note: A label is active when it belongs to one of the four model supports and some component is nonzero at a point in the cell. The definition directly supports conservative coverage by all declared supports.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels
rows.plain: Model harmonics active in a cell

rows.fidelity_note: The coupling-group conditions require coverage for active labels and their unresolved partners. Checking the same coverage for every declared support label is sufficient for these clauses.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The tested-row coverage condition quantifies over active model labels. It is the third consumer of the active-label set identified in the sentence.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowFunctionalConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The harmonic expansion requires the component, temporal-frequency and azimuthal-order triples to be distinct. This is the exact orthogonality requirement stated in the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.IsBoxUniform
ties.plain: Fixed data across the parameter set

rows.fidelity_note: The full bounding data are equal to their central value for every parameter in K. This transports the harmonic supports and all associated bounds together.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.IsBoxUniform
rows.plain: Fixed data across the parameter set

rows.fidelity_note: The fitted-direction set is empty for every selected adjoint. All bounds quantified over that set are therefore vacuous on this specialised route.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.AdjointEntryLinks

rows.fidelity_note: The linked theorem supplies the azimuthal dual estimate by combining the angular inverse-square bound, approximation, mode pairing and time orthogonality. The earlier representation results listed in the sentence are separate results.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.remainderAzimuthalHolds_proof

topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.
topics.name: The fractional extension

topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).
topics.name: The blow-up statements

topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).
topics.name: Passing to the torus

topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).
topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions

topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).
topics.name: Monodromy and the correction

topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).
topics.name: Recurrent profiles

topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).
topics.name: From certificate to profile

topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).
topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate

topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.
topics.name: Encoded cell data

topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).
topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane

topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).
topics.name: Cells, traces and tails

topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).
topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests

topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).
topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound

topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).
topics.name: Changing the profile

topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).
topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error

topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
topics.name: The offset and the certificate
